stories.headline: Governor presents Unit Citations to Air Force Station, Avadi, 27 Special Composite Group of National Security Guard
stories.title: Governor presents Unit Citations to Air Force Station, Avadi, 27 Special Composite Group of National Security Guard
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'national security' in title weight 70
article_sentences: Governor Rajendra Vishwanath Arlekar on Wednesday presented Unit Citations to Air Force Station Avadi and the 27 Special Composite Group (SCG) of the National Security Guard (NSG), Chennai.
The Governor presented the Unit Citations during an event held at Bharathiar Mandapam in Lok Bhavan.
He said that presenting the Unit Citations to the two units was an honour for him, and hailed their collective spirit and unwavering commitment towards serving the nation.
He said the people of the country had the highest regard for the Armed Forces personnel, who not only protected the country’s borders but also saved people during natural disasters.
The Governor also expressed his wish that those aspiring to join government service must be required to undergo two years of military training to ensure dedication and discipline in service.

Air Commodore Pradeep Sharma, Air Officer Commanding, Air Force Station, Avadi; Amit Pathak, Inspector General (Provisioning), NSG; Colonel Ankush Sharma, Group Commander, 27 SCG, NSG, Chennai; Sajjan Singh R. Chavan, Secretary to the Tamil Nadu Governor; and officers of the Armed Forces were present.

stories.headline: US mid-term election outcome effect: G-Secs rally, Rupee gains
stories.title: US mid-term election outcome effect: G-Secs rally, Rupee gains
stories.summary: The Indian rupee extended its winning streak for the fourth consecutive session
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: The Government Securities (G-Secs) market rallied on Wednesday, tracking falling US Treasury yields and dip in crude oil prices amid the Democrats winning control of the US Congress in the mid-term elections.
The rupee too gained ground as the US dollar weakened.

Yield of the widely tracked benchmark 10-year G-Sec (6.94 per cent GS2036) dipped 12 basis points, the biggest single day decline in about six months, to close at 7.19 per cent against the previous close of 7.31 per cent.
The price of this security jumped by about 83 paise.
Yield and prices of a bond are inversely co-related and move in opposite directions.

Referring to the outcome of the US mid-term elections, Nuvama, in report, said: “For Indian government bonds, lower US yields and a weaker dollar could provide external support and improve FPI sentiment in the near term, although domestic factors and crude oil prices will remain key drivers.
For now, 10-year IGB (India Government Bond) has eased.
“But the gains on the US treasury yields may be short lived, and India yields might trade with caution over the near term, given the rally over the past few days from 7.50 per cent to 7.19 per cent.”
At the weekly Treasury Bill (T-Bill) auction, the 91-day and 364-day T-Bill auctions to mobilise ₹8,000 crore and ₹7,000 crore, sailed through.
However, the RBI rejected all bids for the 182-day T-Bill (₹8,000 crore) auction as market participants demanded higher yields.

Meanwhile, the rupee appreciated to a two-week high as the dollar weakened after the US mid-term elections showed the Democrats gaining an upper hand in the US Congress and a decline in crude oil prices.
The Indian unit closed at 94.64/65 per US dollar against the previous close of 94.74/75.

stories.headline: AI stocks retreat as Democratic sweep puts data centre boom in focus
stories.title: AI stocks retreat as Democratic sweep puts data centre boom in focus
stories.summary: Wall Street's rally following the Democratic sweep of Congress did not extend to several companies riding the AI boom. Data centre builders and related technology stocks fell on Wednesday as investors weighed the possibility of greater political scrutiny of the industry's rapid expansion, Bloomberg reports.CoreWeave, Iren and Nebius declined, while power equipment makers GE Vernova and Vertiv also came under pressure. Chipmakers Nvidia and Marvell Technology slipped even as the Nasdaq 100 rose more than 1%.For live updates on US Markets, click here The election has brought concerns about rising electricity bills and AI-driven job losses into sharper focus. Meanwhile, investors were already questioning whether the industry's debt-fuelled spending can be sustained. According to Bloomberg, analysts do not expect political pressure to derail AI development, it could slow the pace of data centre expansion and investment.Also Read: Democrats’ Senate win could shield Federal Reserve from Trump’s influence, but risks persist“The Democrats will not in my opinion challenge what has already been implemented to win this race when it comes to AI. Because there is now a big competition between China and the US when it comes to technology,” Mabrouk Chetouane, Head of Global Market Strategy at Natixis Investment Managers, told Bloomberg.“Some of the questions on data centers suggested concerns about regulation should be faded, but others suggested they should remain in the spotlight. Regardless of what does or does not happen with Congress on this issue, risk does remain from the governors’ results as AI/data centers was a top issue in the close campaigns for those seats,” Lori Calvasina, Head of US Equity Strategy at RBC Capital Markets, said.“We still struggle to support the idea that the election will be a major clearing event for markets, however, given the absence of the usual turbulence in the US equity market around the election so far.”“This does add uncertainty about the path forward and maybe the pace forward, but ultimately we still think that the data center build-out will continue. Maybe the pace changes on the margin, but we ultimately think there’s huge demand for compute and that there may be some changes in how the data centers have to approach this, meaning maybe some of the tax incentives change, maybe some of the counties that really voted against this, maybe they have to move, go somewhere else. They might have to find other alternatives. But we think ultimately — much like fracking — we still expect that we see a buildout. It just may be done with some different concessions, with some guardrails, more guardrails than we had before,” Kieth Lerner, Chief Investment Officer and Chief Market Strategist at Truist Advisory Services, was quoted as saying by Bloomberg.“Republicans or Democrats sitting in any state around the country, not just Texas, look at a state that historically has been Republican friendly with a largely effective governor, seeing them overthrown on this basis that data centers are an unpopular position. I think politicians, if anything, love to get reelected before they think about policy. And so more and more, whether it be Republican or Democrat, are likely to jump on that bandwagon to air quotes protect their state from data centers. Obviously that is a popular narrative,” Brad Long, Chief Investment Officer at Wealthspire, said.“It’s certainly not going to change the fact that data centers will be built out and there’s a lot of demand and there’s a lot of backlog. The question will be the regulation and the time and the throughput there. What markets are going to have to digest is, it’s not will data centers be built, but where and how long will it take and how much red tape will be there? Which obviously pushes further out not just all the capex spending, but the throughput on the benefit from AI,” said Matt Maley, Chief Market Strategist at Miller Tabak + Co.“The headwinds are getting a little bit bigger for the AI movement. That’s going to give us some tough sledding. So it may be a lot harder for the market to see the usual year-end rally in the midterm election years. The ‘not in my backyard’ with data centers is gonna be a 2028 issue immediately, and I think that the 2028 campaign starts today. ... It is all but impossible for the Republicans to win the presidency or win the Electoral College without winning Texas,” he added.“Narrative-wise, I think the initial ‘Glass Half-Full’ post ‘Blue Tsunami’ midterm Elections -trade is based upon the following rationalizations—some probably obvious, some more nuanced: A belief that the election results will lead to a forced moderation of US datacenter buildout, which then calms concerns around the Hyperscaler Capex race-to-infinity ‘prisoner’s dilemma’…Which from a markets-perspective reduces some of financing concerns around magnitude of credit and equities issuance, slows the “FCF burn” -trajectory fears,” said Charlie McElligott, Cross Asset Strategist at Nomura Holdings Inc.“There’s definitely some fears about what this might mean for the AI build-out, especially on data centers, and those names have already been under pressure because of the expected Democratic victory. But I think it’s probably a little bit overblown. It’s going to put more onus on the states, but I don’t think that that will impact existing projects all that much. But it could result in higher cost of production if these companies have to provide maybe more local assistance or navigate more regulation across the board just to get some of these projects through. But we still need these data centers,” JP Powers, Chief Investment Officer at RWA Wealth Partners, told Bloomberg.“You could read this as a vote against data centers, but at some level there’s a lot of momentum toward building them, there’s a lot of jobs at stake. The boulder’s already rolling down the hill to some extent, so the election of a few governors and a change in Congress is not going to completely stop the momentum,” Steve Sosnick, Chief Strategist at Interactive Brokers, said.“The market’s been expressing very valid fears that the money is just being spent too aggressively and that the borrowing is so extreme. And so maybe this slows it down to something that’s a bit more manageable, which isn’t great for the suppliers, but may actually impose a little financial discipline on the industry that markets are okay with.”“This is a wake up call. They have to really get out and make their case why communities should want data centers. I think in the end they will be successful, but it probably slows some of these projects down,” Peter Tchir, Head of Macro Strategy at Academy Securities, said.“Gov-elect Hinojosa favors an immediate moratorium on data center builds in Texas until new laws can be passed to establish guardrails. One interpretation is that existing builds / permits would be free to continue and all new construction would be halted and thus would move to other states. Another interpretation is that the datacenter build is slowing and likely reducing capex; this theme had been building into the election,” Andrew Tyler, Head of Global Market Intelligence at JPMorgan Chase & Co., told Bloomberg. “We would not abandon the Tech trade and would play for a tactical rebound, but we may see the market become increasingly selective of Tech / AI winners and losers.” (Disclaimer: This article is based on inputs from agencies. These do not represent the views of The Economic Times)

stories.headline: Supreme Court flags fertility decline, refers two-child rule to larger bench
stories.title: Supreme Court flags fertility decline, refers two-child rule to larger bench
stories.summary: Supreme Court flags fertility decline, refers two-child rule to larger bench
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
event term: 'supreme court' in summary weight 26.4
article_sentences: Referring to other countries grappling with declining and ageing populations, the top court said India could not afford to ignore the changing demographic trends simply because it already had a large population.

The Supreme Court on Wednesday questioned the continued relevance of laws disqualifying people with more than two children from contesting local body elections, saying the fear of overpopulation that once justified such restrictions had weakened amid changing demographic realities.

Warning that the effects of slowing population growth could be difficult to reverse, the court stressed the need to guard against a potentially irreversible decline in fertility, news agency PTI reported.

A bench of Justices P S Narasimha and Alok Aradhe said the relevance and justification of legislation must be assessed in light of contemporary social conditions rather than solely on the circumstances prevailing when it was enacted.
"Adapting to change is important for achieving justice, as failure to adapt produces injustice and is, in a sense, an abuse of power.
Thus, failure to use power to adapt to change is in its own way an abuse of power," the bench said.

The observations came while hearing a plea by Mangala Bhimrao Ingle, whose election as sarpanch of Kakoda gram panchayat in Maharashtra was set aside on the ground that she had more than two children.
Her disqualification was based on Section 14(1)(j-1) of the Maharashtra Village Panchayats Act, 1959.
The court said a law enacted to address a particular social problem could cease to serve its intended purpose if the circumstances underlying it changed substantially.

The bench referred to the Supreme Court's July 2003 judgment in Javed vs State of Haryana, which upheld provisions of the Haryana Panchayati Raj Act, 1994, disqualifying people with more than two living children from contesting or holding panchayat positions.
It noted that India's total fertility rate (TFR) had declined from 3.0 in 2003 to 1.9, underlining the need to revisit policies framed around population control.
"The need of the hour is to have policies in tune with the present realities.

stories.headline: One Factor I Consider For Elevation Is How Judge Would Be A Team Player In Supreme Court : CJI Surya Kant
stories.title: One Factor I Consider For Elevation Is How Judge Would Be A Team Player In Supreme Court : CJI Surya Kant
stories.summary: With so much filings, Supreme Court is virtually playing a T20 match, CJI said, at the SCBA felicitation for the newly elevated judges.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
event term: 'supreme court' in summary weight 26.4
article_sentences: With so much filings, Supreme Court is virtually playing a T20 match, CJI said, at the SCBA felicitation for the newly elevated judges.

Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant on Wednesday (November 4) said that one of the factors he considers while recommending judges for elevation to the Supreme Court is their ability to function as a team member, given the increasing workload and filings before the apex court.

“One of the factors which at least I have always kept in mind is how you are going to perform as a team member because Supreme Court is virtually now playing a T20 match with this much filing,” the CJI said.

He made the remarks while addressing a felicitation function organised by the Supreme Court Bar Association (SCBA) for the newly appointed judges - Justice Sunita Agarwal and Justice Aparesh Kumar Singh, who took oath on October 6.

Explaining the considerations involved in judicial appointments to the Supreme Court, CJI Surya Kant said that seniority, performance, regional representation and diversity are among the factors weighed by the Collegium.
He observed that the enormous increase in filings reflected the growing public trust in the judiciary, while also contributing to rising pendency.
The CJI also emphasised the importance of the relationship between the Bench and the Bar in the development of law.

“The bar contributes to the development of law, not merely by presenting arguments in court, but by bringing independent perspectives, rigorous research and professional insight to the court's consideration.
The bench in turn must remain open to persuasion and constructive criticism,” he said.

Describing elevation to the Supreme Court as the beginning of a different kind of responsibility, CJI Surya Kant said that the transition involved a change not merely in position but also in the scale and reach of judicial responsibility.

He commended Justice Sunita Agarwal for her administrative capabilities, particularly her work on judicial infrastructure in Gujarat, describing her as “a hardcore administrator” in addition to being a judge.
Recalling Justice Aparesh Kumar Singh's tenure as Chief Justice of the Telangana High Court, the CJI referred to an old matter pending for over 10-12 years which was decided during his tenure.

stories.headline: US sanctions Indian couple, 9 firms over alleged Iran oil trade fraud
stories.title: US sanctions Indian couple, 9 firms over alleged Iran oil trade fraud
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: The United States on Wednesday imposed sanctions on an India-based businessman, his wife and several Indian companies for allegedly helping Iran evade international restrictions on its oil trade through a network involved in maritime fraud.

The US Treasury Department identified Suniel Kumar Sharma and his wife, Jaspreet Preeti Shahid, as the alleged operators of a "vast criminal network" that provided false flags and fraudulent maritime certifications to vessels transporting Iranian petroleum.
The network allegedly helped sanctioned ships, including those operating on behalf of Iran's military and its proxies, continue their operations.
The sanctions were announced under the Trump administration's "Operation Economic Outcast", which aims to cut off Iran's ability to generate revenue through oil exports and other economic activities.

The US Treasury also named Indian nationals Ashwani Kumar Dhiman and Ishwinder Singh, who it said served as directors of businesses associated with Sharma's network, along with nine India-based entities linked to the network.
In a post on X, the US Treasury said Sharma and Shahid had supported Iran's shadow fleet through a web of maritime fraud.
It alleged that their operations provided false flags and certifications to sanctioned vessels involved in transporting Iranian petroleum, including ships working for Iran's military and its proxies.
According to the US Treasury, Sharma and Shahid operated the network from Chandigarh and allegedly established fraudulent maritime registries by impersonating the authorities of several countries.

AFP reported that the couple's operations involved creating websites that falsely claimed to provide ship registration, flagging, seafarer training and vessel classification services on behalf of different countries without their authorisation.
The alleged operations date back to 2014, when the couple reportedly attempted to impersonate the maritime flagging authority of the Caribbean nation of Dominica.
In 2023, Sharma established Singapore-based Eswatini Maritime Affairs and International Ship Registry PTE Ltd.
Despite being publicly disowned by Eswatini authorities, the organisation allegedly continued providing registration services to vessels transporting Iranian oil.
